newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast jet fuel leads gain in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast jet fuel leads gain in late trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast jet fuel prices led late gains in spot products, traders said, as higher futures and a firmer Asian jet market lent support.
"The only market we saw with continuous activity was jet," a broker said, adding that cargoes would likely head to a higher-priced Far Eastern market soon.
NYMEX rallies gave West Coast values an early boost, with January heating oil ending the day 3.11 cents a gallon higher at 74.82 cents amid concerns that cold weather would cause tightness in supply.
Gasoline futures for January ended the day 2.48 cents a gallon higher at 69.52 cents.
West Coat spot trade followed NYMEX, brokers said, with a cargo of January gasoline selling in Los Angeles for 71 cents.
A cargo of December jet fuel sold for 77.25 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, while a January parcel was traded at 76 cents.
NYMEX heat helped lift low sulphur diesel half a cent from the morning to 69.50/70.50 cents a gallon.
Conventional grade gasoline in L.A. remained 69.75/70.75 cents after rising 1.75 cents a gallon in early trade.
CARB-grade gasoline added another 0.75 cents a gallon to early gains, trading late between 71.50 cents and 72.50 cents a gallon.
